subject: Zircon3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — incident, mitigation & closure

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T00:12:00Z
Subject: Zircon3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — we are investigating

Samir —

Thanks for flagging this via the portal. We observed an elevated rate of 5xx and request timeouts originating from the Zircon3b model around 23:40–00:20 UTC last night that correlated with increased tail latencies across a subset of our serving fleet.

We're actively investigating and have Ops on a hot path. Immediate actions we are taking:
- Isolating the affected Zircon3b pools and shifting new requests to unaffected capacity where possible
- Temporarily increasing circuit-breaker sensitivity for Zircon3b routes to reduce error propagation
- Collecting traces and KV/decoder cache dumps for root cause analysis

Can you confirm impact on Widgetly — e.g., UI/API errors or webhook failures — and any specific time windows you saw? If you have a recent example trace id it would help us correlate.

I will send a status update within 30–45 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we understand how disruptive this is and will prioritize.

— Rafael

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T02:00:00Z
Subject: RE: Zircon3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial triage and mitigation

Team —

Summary of findings from Ops triage (00:30–01:45 UTC):
- Symptom: burst of 5xx (502/504) and timeouts localized to a subset of Zircon3b serving hosts. Error traces show OOB accesses while reading KV-cache indices.
- Root cause (so far): a recent heuristic change to the KV cache eviction policy (deployed in canary last week) can under high-concurrency + long-prefix inputs produce inconsistent index pointers; on these hosts it triggers OOB reads and propagated 5xx.

Mitigation applied (01:00 UTC):
1) Immediate traffic steering: we shifted Widgetly and other impacted customers to zircon-quant-3b pools (quantized variant) and to standby Zircon pools that did not receive the canary heuristic. This reduced error rates to baseline at ~01:08 UTC.
2) Circuit-breaker: increased sensitivity for Zircon3b to fail fast and avoid cascading retries.
3) Rollback path: Ops initiated an expedited rollback of the eviction heuristic change in the runtime image on affected hosts; hotfix rollout started at 01:15 UTC.

Next steps:
- Ben to finish the hotfix rollout and confirm host-level metrics by 02:30 UTC. (Ben)
- Launch full integration regression of cache heuristics against long-tail prompts. (Engineering lead — will follow up.)
- Customer comms: Rafael to confirm Widgetly routing and propose service credit. (Rafael)

Attachments: mitigation-checklist-raf-0623.pdf — includes steps for traffic steering, rollback checklist, and validation queries.

Low-friction notes to sales/CS: recommend offering Widgetly a one-time 10% service credit for the window 23:40–01:10 UTC and a technical RCA call.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Zircon3b incident — root cause, actions taken, and closure

Samir —

Following up with the post-incident summary and formal closure for the Zircon3b elevated error window you and others experienced on 2028-06-15. Thank you for your patience and for providing the trace id — that helped correlate several hosts.

What happened (brief):
- Between 23:40–01:10 UTC on 2028-06-15 we saw elevated 5xx and timeouts affecting Zircon3b traffic on a subset of hosts. The immediate customer impact for Widgetly matched what you reported: intermittent UI errors and delayed webhooks.

Root cause (engineering RCA):
- A recently deployed change to the KV cache eviction heuristic produced inconsistent index pointers under a specific high-concurrency + long-prefix prompt workload. Those inconsistencies caused out-of-bounds reads in the serving runtime which surfaced as 5xx errors.

Fixes and mitigation performed:
- Immediate: shifted affected customers (including Widgetly) to zircon-quant-3b and unaffected Zircon pools (completed ~01:08 UTC).
- Short-term: increased circuit-breaker sensitivity to reduce retries and cascading failures.
- Hotfix: rolled back the offending heuristic and deployed a corrected runtime image across affected hosts (completed by 02:40 UTC).
- Long-term: we added regression tests for long-prefix prompt shapes and hardened KV index validations; we also gated the heuristic behind a stricter canary rollout process.

Customer impact and remediation offer:
- We propose a one-time 10% credit for your billing window 2028-06-15 23:40–01:10 UTC. If you prefer a different compensation structure (credits vs. support hours), let me know and we will accommodate.

Attachments and artifacts:
- zircon-incident-log-snippet-0623.txt (excerpts we used to triage)
- mitigation-checklist-raf-0623.pdf
- Full RCA doc: https://drive.redwood.internal/incident/zircon3b-20280615-rca
- Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWI-8721

Would you like a 30-min technical review with our engineering lead this week to walk through the RCA and the regression plan? If so send a few times that work and I will coordinate.

Again, sincerely sorry for the disruption — we take reliability seriously and have already adjusted our rollout and validation practices to reduce recurrence risk.

Best —
